item.title: Canonical Kummerian Kernels in 1-Smooth Pro-$p$ Poincar\'e Duality Groups of Dimension Three
item.description: arXiv:2610.20915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(G,\theta)$ be a finitely generated 1-smooth oriented pro-$p$ group with torsion-free orientation, and suppose that $G$ is a Poincar\'e duality pro-$p$ group of dimension three. The orientation determines a canonical closed normal subgroup $K_\theta(G)$ contained in the Frattini subgroup, and for a Kummerian pair the quotient $G/K_\theta(G)$ is the maximal $\theta$-abelian quotient. We prove that \[K_\theta(G)\text{ finitely generated} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad K_\theta(G)=1.\] Thus every non-$\theta$-abelian 1-smooth $\textrm{PD}^3$ pro-$p$ group has an infinitely generated canonical kernel, where ``infinitely generated'' means not topologically finitely generated. The proof combines the normal-subgroup theorem for pro-$p$ $\textrm{PD}^3$ groups with the classification of $p$-adic analytic 1-smooth pro-$p$ groups. We also obtain a cohomological description of the canonical extension from the Hochschild--Serre five-term sequence and Poincar\'e duality. Writing $K=K_\theta(G)$, $Q=G/K$, and $V=H^1(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$, we identify $H^1(K,\mathbb{F}_p)^Q$ with the kernel of the map $\bigwedge^2V\to V^*$ induced by the triple cup-product form of $G$. Consequently, whenever $K\neq1$, its first cohomology is infinite-dimensional, whereas its $Q$-invariant subspace is nonzero and finite-dimensional. We obtain exact dimension restrictions in small generator ranks and show that a non-$\theta$-abelian group with $2\leq d(G)\leq4$ is not Bloch--Kato. In the finitely generated-kernel case, $G$ is a three-dimensional uniform $\theta$-abelian group with exterior mod-$p$ cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Marina Palaisti

item.title: Resolutions of orbifold generalised triangle groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.20932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}=1\rangle$ be a generalised triangle group in which $W$ is the Farey word of a rational slope $q=r/s$, and suppose that $T$ is the fundamental group of a hyperbolic $3$-orbifold whose singular locus has no spherical vertices. Let $G=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}\rangle$ be the associated central extension. We compute an explicit free resolution of the trivial module over $\mathbb{Z}G$ of minimal length, with differentials given in closed form by Fox derivatives. From this resolution we deduce an explicit free resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ which is $2$-periodic in degrees at least two, and we compute the integral homology and cohomology of both groups. Strebel treated the classical family $q=0/1$ in 1983. Since then only the family $q=1/2$ has been treated, by Ellis and Williams, and for that family our resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ has strictly smaller rank in every degree.
item.dc:creator: Sean P. Carroll, Thomas Csizmadia, Jeroen Schillewaert

item.title: Quadratic fields of values of finite solvable groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.20992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that if $G$ is a finite solvable group such that $E = \mathbb Q(\{\chi(g)\, |\, \chi\in{\rm Irr}(G),\ g \in G\})$ is an extension of degree 2 over the rationals, then $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{\pm d})$ for a positive integer $d$ all of whose prime divisors lie in $\{2, 3, 5\}$. Moreover, if $G$ has a composition factor of order 7, then either $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{2})$ or $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. This provides a partial answer to a question of G. Navarro.
item.dc:creator: Sara C. Deb\'on, Joan F. Tent

item.title: Automorphisms of twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over local rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.20994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over commutative local rings with involution and $2$ invertible, for both isogeny types. Every automorphism is standard, with no invertibility assumption on $3$. In the adjoint case, it has a unique expression as a composition of conjugation by an element of the full twisted group and a ring automorphism commuting with the involution. For the simply connected form, the full group equals its elementary subgroup, and the factors are strictly inner, diagonal, and ring automorphisms. The main step replaces a linear change of basis by a group element. Invariant alternating tensors determine the transported Chevalley bracket. We correct this bracket over a faithfully flat local extension and descend the resulting conjugating element by uniqueness. Root-subgroup relations then recover the coefficient automorphism.
item.dc:creator: Elena I. Bunina, Deep H. Makadiya

item.title: A simultaneous variant of the Hall-Paige theorem and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.21600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $k\geq 1$ , we say that a finite group $G$ satisfies property $\mathcal P_k$ if, for every $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_k\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$, there exists a bijection $f$ of $G$ such that each map $g\mapsto \beta_i(g)f(g)$ is a bijection. For $k=1$ this is equivalent to the classical Hall--Paige complete mapping property. We prove that if $p$ is the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, then $G$ satisfies $\mathcal P_k$ for every $k<p-1$ and we show that this bound is sharp. For finite abelian $p$-groups, the bijection $f$ may moreover be chosen to be an automorphism, and for noncyclic homocyclic $p$-groups this remains true for $k=p-1$. Finally, we interpret $\mathcal P_k$ in terms of common transversals and common orthogonal mates of Latin squares generated from automorphisms and the Cayley table of a finite group $G$.
item.dc:creator: Maria Loukaki

item.title: Two-element factors and finite bases for additively idempotent semirings
item.description: arXiv:2610.21605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every additively idempotent semiring $S$ in the constant-free signature, $S$ is finitely based if and only if $S\times E$ is finitely based when $E=M_2$ or $T_2$. For each $E\in\{L_2,R_2,D_2,N_2\}$, both implications fail in general: we give a finitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is nonfinitely based and a nonfinitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is finitely based.
item.dc:creator: Qirui Ma, Mengya Yue

item.title: Automorphisms of triality groups over local rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.21662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative local ring with $2,3\in R^\times$, and let $\rho\in\Aut(R)$ satisfy $\rho^3=\id$. We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full triality groups in the adjoint and simply connected forms of type $D_4$. Every automorphism is uniquely determined by an adjoint group element and a ring automorphism preserving the trace $T=\id+\rho+\rho^2$; conversely, every such pair defines an automorphism. A square-zero example shows that trace-preserving coefficient automorphisms need not normalize $\langle\rho\rangle$ when $\rho$ is nontrivial on $R$ but trivial on its residue field. We also prove a relative rigidity theorem for homomorphisms from elementary triality groups over arbitrary coefficient rings to local targets with $2$ and $3$ invertible, assuming that an adjoint conjugation makes the parameter-one root images standard modulo the maximal ideal. Conversely, every unital trace-preserving ring homomorphism into such a local coefficient ring induces the corresponding homomorphism of elementary groups.
item.dc:creator: Elena Bunina, Avi Berezovskiy, Deep Makadiya

item.title: Only their cardinality can prevent groups from being quotients of weakly branch groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is a well-known fact that every proper quotient of a branch group is a virtually abelian group. We record that every group of cardinality at most $2^{\aleph_0}$ is a quotient of a weakly branch group; in fact, there are weakly branch groups that are split extensions with free complements. Furthermore, if a group is generated by $d$ elements, there is a weakly branch group generated by $(d+2)$ elements mapping onto it. As applications of this fact, we resolve a question of Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch but non-branch groups with maximal subgroups of infinite index and, partially, a question of Cox and Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch groups that are not invariably generated.
item.dc:creator: J. Moritz Petschick

item.title: Locally indicable groups outside Brodski\u{i}'s quasivariety
item.description: arXiv:2610.22121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a set of group properties that together obstruct membership in the quasivariety that Brodski\u{i} constructed in his proof that torsion-free one-relator groups are locally indicable. There are examples of locally indicable groups with these properties, which implies that Brodski\u{i}'s quasivariety is strictly contained in the quasivariety of all locally indicable groups. This disproves a conjecture of Howie.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Bo{\ss}

item.title: Applications of $C^*$-Entropy to Representation Growth for Discrete Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The topological $1$-bounded entropy $h^\text{top}(C^*(\Gamma))$ of the full group $C^*$-algebra of a finitely generated group $\Gamma$ is given a representation-theoretic interpretation. The implications of Hilbert-Schmidt and matricial stability in this setting are investigated, recovering and strengthening a representation growth result of Hadwin and Shulman. The entropy framework is used to recover upper bounds on representation growth for superrigid groups and property (T) groups. This recovers a result of De La Harpe, Robinson, and Valette on the growth rate of the irreducible unitary representations of a property (T) group within the framework of $1$-bounded entropy. A soft proof that $SL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ admits subexponential representation growth is recorded.
item.dc:creator: Connor MacMahon

item.title: Random Quotients of Hyperbolic Spaces with Respect to WPD Actions and Linear Connectivity of the Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.21141v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study random quotients of acylindrically hyperbolic groups and hierchically hyperbolic groups, whose (partial) hyperbolicity is captured by their actions on Gromov hyperbolic spaces. We show that if an acylindrically hyperbolic group $G$ acts on a Gromov hyperbolic space $X$ coarsely transitively with a WPD element, then the quotient of $X$ by the normal closure of a random element of $G$ has linearly connected boundary. If $G$ is a group with a (relative) hierarchically hyperbolic group structure, with a quasi-tree top domain $X$, then in fact the quotient of $X$ by the normal closure of a random element of $G$ has boundary homeomorphic to the N\"obeling curve.
item.dc:creator: Inhyeok Choi, Henry Talbott

item.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $\Gamma$ satisfies $\exp(\Gamma) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.
item.dc:creator: Kengo Enami, Takahiro Matsushita

item.title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
item.description: arXiv:2610.21954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.
item.dc:creator: Ualbai Umirbaev

item.title: Multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures of generalized Johnson association schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak X$ be a commutative association scheme of class $d$ on $X$. We construct the generalized Johnson association scheme $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ on partial maps from $[n]$ to $X$ with domains of size $h$. For $1\le h\le n-1$, we prove that $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ has $(d+1)$-variate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. In particular, its multivariate $Q$-polynomial property answers affirmatively a problem posed for generalized Johnson association schemes arising from finite Gelfand pairs. We also determine the primitive idempotents and the two eigenmatrices, expressing the first eigenmatrix as a product of an Eberlein polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial, and the second eigenmatrix as a product of a Hahn polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial. For the multivariate factors, we use Mizukawa--Tanaka $(d+1,2d+2)$-hypergeometric functions. In an appendix, we identify the normalized columns of the second eigenmatrix with the known spherical functions in the finite Gelfand pair case. We also discuss the orthogonality relations and the imprimitivity arising from partial maps with the same domain, and explicitly describe the multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures inherited by the blocks and the quotient.
item.dc:creator: Hirotake Kurihara

item.title: Global transfer systems and endopurity of subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.22141v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Global transfer systems are combinatorial objects that parametrize intermediate levels of structures and properties in globally equivariant homotopy theory. In this paper we study the lattice of global transfer systems, expanding beyond the case of abelian groups which was computed by the second author. The main result is a proof that the irreducible elements of the lattice of global transfer systems are strictly controlled by subgroups of groups which we refer to as endopure. From the irreducible elements one can recover the whole lattice, and studying these endopure subgroups leads us to a wide range of new phenomena and computations.
item.dc:creator: Scott Balchin, Miguel Barrero

item.title: Uniform Intersection Numbers and Subgroup-Based Generating Graphs of Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.22268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The uniform intersection number of a finite group $G$, denoted by $ui(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that the intersection of any $k$ distinct maximal subgroups of $G$ is equal to its Frattini subgroup. We determine the uniform intersection number of dicyclic, dihedral, and quasi-dihedral groups. We then investigate the uniform intersection number through the subgroup-based generating graph $\mathcal{G}(G)$ of a finite group $G$. We characterize the finite groups $G$ for which both the intersection number and the uniform intersection number are equal to two, and show that this condition is equivalent to $\mathcal{G}(G)$ being complete multipartite. We also classify finite groups in terms of the diameter, girth, and perfectness of $\mathcal{G}(G)$. Finally, we show that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ is Hamiltonian if and only if $n=p_1^{r}p_2^{r}$, where $r\geq 2$ and $p_1$ and $p_2$ are distinct primes.
item.dc:creator: Projesh Nath Choudhury, Biswaranjan Khanra

item.title: On a theorem of Artin and the dimension of the space spanned by the rational valued characters of a group
item.description: arXiv:2601.12185v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we sharpen a theorem of Artin to show that for a finite group, the dimension of the subspace of class functions spanned by the rational valued characters equals the number of conjugacy classes of cyclic subgroups.
item.dc:creator: Mark L. Lewis

item.title: Generation of Iterated Wreath Products Constructed from Almost Simple Groups
item.description: arXiv:2602.03830v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let G1, G2, ... be a sequence of almost simple groups and construct a sequence (Wi) of wreath products via W1 = G1 and, for each i > 1, Wi+1 = Gi+1 wr Wi via the regular action of each Gi. We determine the minimum number d(Wi) of generators required for each wreath product in this sequence.
item.dc:creator: Jiaping Lu

item.title: Common overlattices in trees and trees with fins
item.description: arXiv:2602.14646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bass and Kulkarni proved that any pair of free uniform lattices in the automorphism group of a tree have conjugates that both lie inside a third uniform lattice (which is not necessarily free). We show that this does not generalise to trees with fins. The construction of our counter-example involves working with a certain generalisation of the universal groups of Burger and Mozes.
item.dc:creator: Sam Shepherd

item.title: Profinite isomorphisms, stable commutator length, and fixed point properties
item.description: arXiv:2603.12095v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct Grothendieck pairs witnessing that stable commutator length and quasimorphisms are not profinite invariants, answering a question of Echtler and Kammeyer. Moreover, we recover the fact that property FA, property NL (which obstructs actions on hyperbolic spaces), and property FW$_\infty$ (which obstructs actions on finite-dimensional CAT(0) cube complexes) and the existence of non-abelian free subgroups are not profinite invariants. The method combines Rips constructions with iterated group-theoretic Dehn filling on hyperbolic virtually special groups.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Fournier-Facio

item.title: Classifying Prime Character Degree Graphs With Eight Vertices
item.description: arXiv:2603.15851v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, an effort is made to classify which prime character degree graphs having eight vertices occur for some finite solvable group. To approach this, we compile known results and constructions from the literature which are used to develop a general algorithm to begin classifying graphs of any order. We then apply the algorithm to the graphs of order eight. Of the 12,346 non-isomorphic graphs with eight vertices, 1,229 are disconnected and are fully classified. Meanwhile, thirty-seven of the 11,117 non-isomorphic connected graphs are shown to occur; thirty-four of which are constructed via joins of smaller graphs and three of which have diameter three. Fifty-eight graphs are shown not to occur, several of which fall into previously studied families, while the classification of 204 graphs is still unknown.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: journal of Groups, complexity, cryptology, Volume 18 Issue 2 (October 9, 2026) gcc:18044
item.dc:creator: Mark L. Lewis, Andrew Summers

item.title: Non-split sharply 2- and 3-transitive groups in SL_n(\mathbb Z)
item.description: arXiv:2604.07001v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ contains a non-split sharply 2-transitive subgroup, answering a question of Glasner and Gulko. We also prove that $\mathrm{SL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ contains a non-split sharply 3-transitive subgroup, but that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ does not contain an infinite sharply 3-transitive subgroup.
item.dc:creator: Marco Amelio, Simon Andr\'e

item.title: Green languages and growth of free inverse monoids
item.description: arXiv:2609.35251v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by recent work on conjugacy languages in groups, we introduce a general framework for studying \emph{languages of representatives} associated to equivalence relations on finitely generated semigroups. After developing this notion in full generality, we particularize it to Green's relations and obtain the corresponding Green languages, which form the central objects of this article. For free inverse monoids, we describe these languages via Munn trees and establish several structural relations among them, including characterizations of the $\mathcal{D}$-, $\mathcal{R}$-, $\mathcal{L}$-, and $\mathcal{H}$-languages. We then investigate the formal language-theoretic complexity of these Green languages. For free inverse monoids of rank at least two, we show that $\mathcal{H}$-Geo is context-free and co-context-free but not regular, while $\mathcal{R}$-Geo, $\mathcal{L}$-Geo, and $\mathcal{D}$-Geo are neither context-free nor co-context-free. In contrast, in the monogenic case, $\mathcal{D}$-Geo is regular and the remaining Green languages are deterministic context-free. We further relate these results to the ShortLex language and the growth of free inverse monoids, proving in particular that $(\text{FIM}_X,X)$ is growth tight. The article concludes with a collection of open problems and directions for future research.
item.dc:creator: Corentin Bodart, Andr\'e Carvalho, Ana-Catarina C. Monteiro

item.title: The theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations of groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15826v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by recent work on $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations as combinatorial structures with prescribed representation multiplicities. Such a factorization consists of two subsets of a finite group whose products represent each nonidentity element exactly $\lambda$ times and the identity exactly $\mu$ times. These structures generalize $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations and provide a common framework for several families arising in combinatorial design theory, including strong external difference families with two equal-sized subsets, as well as binary sequence pairs with two-level correlation. Their associated $\{0,1\}$-matrices satisfy the Bridges-Ryser equation $XY=\lambda(J-I)+\mu I$, linking the factorization problem to a classical matrix framework for combinatorial designs. We establish the foundational theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Donald L. Kreher, Shuxing Li, Douglas R. Stinson

item.title: Optimal Transport on Lie Group Orbits
item.description: arXiv:2508.09377v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In its most general form, the optimal problem is an infinite-dimensional optimization problem, yet certain notable instances admit closed-form solutions. We identify the common source of this tractability as \textit{symmetry} and formalize it using Lie group theory. Fixing a Lie group action and a reference distribution, we study optimal transport between measures in the same orbit. For such pairs of measures, restricting the Monge problem to transport maps induced by the group action yields the Lie group orbit transport problem, an optimization over the stabilizer of the reference law that provides an upper bound on the Monge problem. Under suitable regularity conditions, a feasible group-induced map satisfying a $c$-convex first-order certificate attains this bound, solves the original Monge problem, and induces an optimal Kantorovich plan. For the quadratic cost, we establish a structural criterion based on a global Cartan decomposition. Exploiting the nonuniqueness of orbit representations, the criterion constructs an optimal map through a path of group transformations with self-adjoint derivatives. Once verified for an action and reference law, it applies to every pair of orbit measures with finite second moments. For affine-induced actions, Cartan structure on the linear image suffices, and the means and covariance operators determine the optimal map and value explicitly. The framework recovers classical elliptical transport formulas and yields closed-form solutions on congruence orbits generated by absolutely continuous, spectrally invariant reference laws, including Wishart, inverse-Wishart, and matrix beta type~II families with fixed shape parameters. It also recovers the common-copula optimal coupling for multivariate normal sinh-arcsinh laws with unit tailweight parameters sharing a Gaussian copula, and evaluates the optimal transport value in closed form.
item.dc:creator: Bahar Taskesen

item.title: The Multiorbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial: A Subgroup-Lattice Refinement
item.description: arXiv:2609.01866v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomial F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}\sum_{h\in H}P_{\Gamma/h}(x,y), which aggregates the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials associated with all subgroups of a finite group acting on a graph. We derive the equivalent element-wise representation F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{g\in G}c_G(g)P_{\Gamma/g}(x,y), where c_G(g) = \sum_{\langle g\rangle\leq H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}. The coefficient function depends only on the cyclic subgroup generated by the element and is constant on conjugacy classes. This yields decompositions by cyclic subgroups and conjugacy classes and an interpretation in terms of the incidence algebra of the subgroup lattice. After normalization, the coefficients define a probability distribution obtained by choosing a subgroup uniformly and then an element uniformly from that subgroup. We also establish diagonal multiplicativity for disjoint unions and a weighted cycle-index expression for edgeless graphs. A further contribution concerns the distinguishing power of the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial. We answer a question of Dohmen and Lange-Geisler affirmatively by exhibiting two non-isomorphic graphs, P_3 and K_2 \mathbin{\dot\cup} K_1 under C_2-actions, with identical orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. The two actions nevertheless have different multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. Thus the multiorbital polynomial is not determined by the orbital bivariate polynomial, whereas the converse question remains open.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Gerling

item.title: Farey Symbols for the Picard Group
item.description: arXiv:2609.36629v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop Picard Farey symbols for finite-index subgroups of \(G=\PSL_2(\ZZ[i])\) from the Gaussian Farey tessellation of \(\HH^3\) by ideal octahedra. The ambient geometry naturally involves two different index-two extensions of \(G\): the orientation-preserving group \(\PGL_2(\ZZ[i])\) and a reflection extension. This distinction explains the two \(G\)-orbits of Farey faces, which merge into one \(\PGL_2\)-orbit, and the classical extended modular tessellation appears as a totally geodesic slice. A Picard Farey symbol records finitely many Gaussian-rational octahedral occurrences, their local stabilizers, and cooriented face-pairing transformations. We prove that such a symbol reconstructs the finite Picard-cell action and hence the subgroup; moreover, when subgroup membership is decidable, the symbol can be found by a terminating finite double-coset procedure. For torsion-free subgroups we obtain whole-octahedron fundamental domains. The marked symbol also supplies finite orbit relations for the established Gaussian Steinberg edge--face presentation, with its corresponding Bianchi modular-symbol relations. When the natural modular-to-Picard coset map is bijective, a side-connected Kulkarni special polygon lifts, using the same modular representatives, to a Picard fundamental polyhedron whose intersection with the invariant real plane is exactly that polygon; the level-$(2+i)$/level-$5$ family is worked out explicitly. Comparison examples show that octahedral boundary minimization, absolute geometric face minimization, and preservation of such a modular section are distinct problems. Canonical reduction and effective Hecke reduction remain open.
item.dc:creator: Devendra Tiwari, Helena Verrill

item.title: Large-scale rank and geometry of the Lipschitz metric on geodesic currents
item.description: arXiv:2610.03359v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a closed orientable surface of genus at least 2, we study the large-scale geometry of the (symmetrized) Lipschitz metric on its space of projective filling geodesic currents. We show that the rank and, hence, asymptotic dimension of the space of filling geodesic currents is infinite. This gives the first example of a natural proper space associated to a closed surface, with a metrically proper isometric action of the mapping class group, that has infinite asymptotic dimension. In contrast, we show that any finite simplex of geodesic currents has rank uniformly bounded above by $8g-9$. We then show a sufficient criterion for its rank and asymptotic dimension to be equal to $8g-9$ and construct examples satisfying it, thus showing the bound is sharp. We further prove that Teichm\"uller space equipped with the Lipschitz metric has rank equal to $3g-3$. In particular, the space of projective filling geodesic currents and the Teichm\"uller space are not quasi-isometric.
item.dc:creator: D\'idac Mart\'inez-Granado, Jenya Sapir
